record.paper_title: Model Theory of Tame Valued Fields and Beyond: Recent Developments and Open Questions
record.context_brief: Elementary equivalence: henselization of F_p(t) vs. F_p((t))
record.original_question: Let p be a prime and let F_p be the field with p elements. Let F_p(t) be the rational function field in one variable t over F_p, with the t-adic valuation v_t (which sends a rational function to the order of vanishing at t = 0). Let (F_p(t)^h, v_t) denote the henselization of (F_p(t), v_t), and let (F_p((t)), v_t) denote the formal Laurent series field over F_p with its t-adic valuation. It is known that (F_p(t)^h, v_t) is existentially closed in (F_p((t)), v_t) in the language L_val of valued rings. Is (F_p(t)^h, v_t) an elementary substructure of (F_p((t)), v_t) in L_val (i.e., do they satisfy exactly the same first-order sentences in L_val)?

evidence.quote: Open problem 6: Is F_p(t)^h an elementary substructure of F_p((t))? In contrast, Jahnke and Kartas prove that F_p(t^{1/p^infty})^h is an elementary substructure of F_p((t))^{1/p^infty}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p$ be a prime number and let $\mathbb{F}_p$ be the finite field with $p$ elements. Let $\mathbb{F}_p(t)$ be the field of rational functions in one variable $t$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$, equipped with the $t$-adic valuation $v_t$ (which assigns to a nonzero rational function its order of vanishing at $t=0$). Let $(\mathbb{F}_p(t)^h, v_t)$ denote the henselization of $(\mathbb{F}_p(t), v_t)$ inside an algebraic closure of $\mathbb{F}_p(t)$, and let $(\mathbb{F}_p((t)), v_t)$ denote the field of formal Laurent series over $\mathbb{F}_p$ with its $t$-adic valuation. Consider these as structures in the first-order language $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{val}}$ of valued rings (a language for rings together with a predicate or sort for the valuation ring/valuation). It is known that $(\mathbb{F}_p(t)^h, v_t)$ is existentially closed in $(\mathbb{F}_p((t)), v_t)$ with respect to $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{val}}$.

Question: Is $(\mathbb{F}_p(t)^h, v_t)$ an elementary substructure of $(\mathbb{F}_p((t)), v_t)$ in the language $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{val}}$? Equivalently, do these two valued fields satisfy exactly the same first-order $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{val}}$-sentences (with parameters from $\mathbb{F}_p(t)^h$)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the henselization of $\mathbb{F}_p(t)$ with the $t$-adic valuation is an elementary substructure of $\mathbb{F}_p((t))$ is a well-known open problem in the model theory of positive-characteristic valued fields. A related perfect-hull variant, namely that $\mathbb{F}_p(t^{1/p^\infty})^h \preceq \mathbb{F}_p((t))^{1/p^\infty}$, has been established by Jahnke and Kartas, but the original (non-perfect) version remains open. Web searches did not turn up any announcement of a resolution.

status_evidence.title: Large implies Henselian
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of model-theoretic properties of henselian valued fields in positive characteristic; the elementary substructure question for F_p(t)^h in F_p((t)) is not reported as resolved.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on henselian valued fields does not announce a solution to the elementary substructure question.
